relations.note: Meretseger is titled Daughter of Re through Eye-of-Re and uraeus theology.
relations.source: TT 106, tomb of Paser, Pillar H

relations.note: Older readings call Meretseger Daughter of the West or Amentet.

other_aliases: Ptah of the Valley of the Queens
relations.myth: Joint worship in the rock-cut sanctuary
relations.note: Meretseger and Ptah jointly receive worship in the western Theban chapel complex.
Separate hymns credit both deities with punishing Neferabu and responding to penitence.
Meretseger was regionally fused with Hathor through shared western, funerary, cobra, and maternal roles.
relations.source: Deir el-Bahri graffito and regional iconography

relations.note: Meretseger and Hathor appear together in local scenes, sometimes as Hathor-Meretseger.
Meretseger assumes Renenutet-like serpent and provider functions without permanent identity.
Anthropomorphic Meretseger presents papyrus to Osiris in a royal chapel scene.
relations.source: Valley of the Queens Chapel B stela

relations.note: Meretseger appears within the Osirian protective world of royal funerary monuments.
Weret-Hekau's identity is layered with Meretseger in a temporary uraeus-goddess composite.
relations.source: TT 106, tomb of Paser, Pillar H

relations.note: Amun-Re, Meretseger, and deified Amenhotep I jointly receive worship.
Meretseger and deified Amenhotep I jointly receive worship as local patrons.

relations.myth: Cultic co-presence in the chapel complex
relations.note: Mut and Meretseger share the broader divine setting of the Valley of the Queens sanctuary.
relations.source: Valley of the Queens royal stelae
